rows.title_full: AN ACT DEFINING TERRORISM, PROVIDING PENALTIES THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: The very grave threat to the Filipino people posed by violent terrorist acts is documented by the events during the past months as well as the past few years.  The attack has prompted the international community to talk about a global effort to eradicate terrorism. We join the call for an international effort to deprive terrorists of their extra-territori al sanctuaries. This is not America's war alone. This is civilized society's war against terrorism. The local terrorists have strengthened themselves by linking up with, and getting support from, international terrorist organizations.> The grave threat to the security of our people - terrorism must be addressed effectively. Our law enforcement agencies must be provided with suffficient tools and training to counter this present-day menace. The proposed bill is designed to improve the substantive provisions of our penal laws to directly address terrorism including the movement of suspected foreign terrorists and their vario
rows.status: Substituted by HB05923

rows.abstract: "Drugs Act of 2001". This bill seeks to STRENGTHEN the mandate of administrative machinery of the DOH and of existing laws regarding drugs and pharmaceuticals . To achieve this, the bill seeks, among others, to introduce vital amendments to existinglaws concerning drugs and pharmaceuticals not only to pave the way for: (1) a greater state intervening through a more active and efficient regulatory system in the drug industry complemented by a more vigorous and intrusive participation of the DOHin the purchase and distribution of drugs as to effectively influence the prevailing price schemes in the market but also (2) in extending the support long clamored by local drug firms.

rows.author: D020
rows.title_full: AN ACT PENALIZING PROSTITUTION, DEFINING THE PERSONS LIABLE THEREFOR, PROVIDING MEASURES AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR ITS VICTIMS, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE THE REVISED PENAL CODE, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: "Anti-Prostitut ion Act." Rationale: Prostitution must be approached in its entirety, interrogating both the structural mechanisms and the ideological justifications which uphold it. In addressing prostitution, the government must address the contradictions in policies which in effect, reinforce the system of prostitution. The adult-child divide must be removed, and women and children in prostitution must be decriminalized alike. The goal of minimizing, if not totally eradicating prostitution,must be directed against establishments and male customers who control and profit from the business of prostitution. Policies and programs must be developed that will address the problems of women in prostitution, provide them protection, penalize thhose who control, perpetuate, and benefit fro, the business of prostitution, address the factors in general that perpetuate prostitution, and serve to eradicate prostitutions in the long term.> Thus, this proposed measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-11-20

rows.abstract: "Optical Media Act of 2001." "OPTICAL MEDIA shall refer to any prerecorded or recordable medium or device on which digital information, including any fixation of sound, images, or any combination of both, or software code, is stored, including various disc formats any technical variation now known or still to be devised in the future, which may be accessed and read using a lens scanning mechanism employing a high intensity light source such as a laser. > It is the policy of the State to ensurethe protection of intellectual property rights by creating an environment conducive to the growth and development of all business industries; that optical media piracy in all form is inimical to economic growth and public intrest; and that therefore,, the State shall institute the means of curtail all forms of optical media piracy.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE PROCLAMATION OF THE CANDIDATE THE NEXT HIGHEST NUMBER OF VOTES FOR THE SAME POSITION AS THE ELECTED CANDIDATES FOR THE POSITION IN CASES OF CANCELLATION OF CERTIFICATE OF CANDIDACY OR QUO WARRANTO CASES OR ANY DISQUALIFICATIO N PROCEEDINGS IF THE CANDIDATE CREDITED WITH THE HIGHEST NUMBER OF VOTES IS DISQUALIFIED OR DECLARED NOT QUALIFIED
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to provide for the proclamation of the candidate obtaining the next highest number of votes for the same position as the elted candidates for the position in cases of cancellation of certificate of candidacy or quo warranto cases orany disqualificatio n proceedings if the candidate credited with the highest number of votes is disqualified or declared not qualified accordingly. > Allowing the proclamation of the candidate who obtained the next highest number of vote in a elective position, in the event that the candidate obtaining the highest number of votes has been disqualified or declared not qualified will hopefully harmonize jurisprudence on election laws.

rows.title_full: AN ACT CREATING THE DEPARTMENT OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY AND COMMUNICATIONS, DEFINING ITS POWERS AND FUNCTIONS, APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: Recognizinf the important role of Information and Communications Technology (ICT) in national development, there is a need to have a concerted effort between the government and the business sector to pursue an ICT development strategy forthe country. The business sector will play the lead role in driving ICT development. The government, on the other hand, will provide an efficient and effective business environment, regulatory framework, and the services needed for ICT to develop and thrive.> Therefore, there is a need for a bill that will create a Department of Information Technology and Communications (DITC) which will be responsbile in providing the policy and legal environment and the institutional mechanisms that will prommote the development of ICT in the country. This Department will also ensure the availability of enabling factors such as infrastructure support, financial resources and qualified/skill ed human resources, etc.

rows.abstract: "Citizenship Retention Act of 2001." rows.title_full: AN ACT AMENDING REPUBLIC ACT NO. 6425, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE DANGEROUS DRUGS ACT OF 1972, AS AMENDED, CLASSIFYING METHYLAMPHETAMI NE HYDROCHLORIDE OR SHABU AS A PROHIBITED DRUG AND IMPOSING THE PENALTIES PROVIDED BY THE SAID ACT FOR THE IMPORTATION, MANUFACTURE, SALE, ADMINISTRATION DELIVERY, DISTRIBUTION AND TRANSPORTATION OF DANGEROUS DRUGS, CULTIVATION OF PLANTS SOURCES OF DANGEROUS DRUGS AND MAINTENANCE OF A DRUG DEN WITHOUT REGARD TO THE QUANTITY OF THE DANGEROUS DRUGS INVOLVED
rows.abstract: Rationale: To improve government efficiency in its fight against dangerous drugs, now is the time that we finetune our laws against illegal drugs, particularly Republic Act 6425, otherwise known as the "The Dangerous Drugs Act of 1972" to the effectthat methlyamphetami ne hydrochloride or shabu be classified as a prohibited drug and that the penalties provided therein for the importation, manufacture, sale, administration, delivery, distribution and transportation of dangerous drugs, the cultivation of plant sources of dangerous drugs and maintenance of a drug den for drug users be imposed without regard to the quantity of dangerous drugs involved, with the end view that the aforementioned offenses be classified as non-bailable and the coonvicts ineligible for probation after conviction.
rows.status: Substituted by HB04433

rows.title_full: AN ACT ALLOCATING TWENTY-FIVE PERCENT (25%) OF TRAVEL TAX COLLECTIONS IN THE COUNTRY TO THE DEVELOPMENT AND PROMOTION OF TOURISM INDUSTRY IN THE TWENTY (20) DEPRESSED PROVINCES
rows.abstract: This bill seeks to allocate twenty-five percent (25%) of the travel tax collections being imposed under Presidential Decree No. 1183 to the development and promotion of tourism in the twenty (20) depressed provinces. > Capitalizing on the enormous potential of the tourism industry, the government has taken bold initiatives to maximize its contribution to the economy through the upgrading of roads, airports and seaports, deregulation of civil aviation, introduction of high-tech telecommunicati on services and brand new transport and recreational facilities. > The government has likewise included in its initiative the development of other potential tourist attractions in all provices, particularly in the twenty (20) depressed provinces identtified by the Office of the President.

rows.author: D044
rows.title_full: AN ACT EXEMPTING PAUPER LITIGANTS AND THOSE SIMILARLY SITUATED FROM POSTING BAIL WHEN CHARGED WITH NON-CAPITAL OFFENSES AND BE RELEASED ON RECOGNIZANCE OF THE PUNONG BARANGAY WHERE HE/SHE RESIDES OR OF ANY RESPONSIBLE PERSON RESIDING IN THE SAID BARANGAY
rows.abstract: "Pauper Litigants Welfare Act of 2001". Rationale: The Constitution assures all persons, except those charged with capital offenses when the evidence of guilt is strong, that they shall, before conviction, be entitled to bail by sufficient suretiesor be released on recognizance as may be provided by law. However, fourteen and a half years after its effectivity, these constitutional provisions have never been fully realized as no enabling legislation has yet been enacted. > This bill seeks to relieve pauper litigants, or those similarly situated, the economic burden of posting bail when charged with non-capital offenses and be released on recognizance of the Punong Barangay of the barangay where he/she is resides, or of any responsible perrson residing in the said barangay.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2001-11-26

rows.abstract: This proposed measure gives to broaden the tax base by granting rebates to any buyer, transferee or lessee of goods, properties or services equivalent to one hundred percent (100%) of the total Value-Added tax imposed for every transaction covered by existing VAT laws. This way, buyers or consumers will be encouraged to demand a receipt or invoice for every purchase of goods for VAT covered transactions, which for many years, had become the primary source of unremitted revenues to the government.

rows.title_full: AN ACT PROVIDING FOR THE RETENTION OF CITIZENSHIP BY PHILIPPINE CITIZENS WHO ACQUIRE FOREIGN CITIZENSHIP, AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE COMMONWEALTH ACT NO. 63, AS AMENDED, AND FOR OTHER PURPOSES
rows.abstract: Rationale: This legislative measure seeks to recognize the reality that hundreds of thousands of natural born Filipinos have lost their citizenship, not through their own volition, but because of the lack of economic opportunity. These Filipinos, scattered throughout the world, have lost their citizenship more by accident than by choice. Even if they are no longer living in the Republic, they shall always remain Filipino in heart and in mind. > This measure would hopefully be a form of recognition to the many faceless Filipinos who are working long hours in far-flung reaches of the world. Their efforts and achievements are just as important and just as valuable to our objective of building a stronger and more prosperous republic.

rows.abstract: The Clean Air Act, RA No. 8749, is amended as follows: "SEC. 20. LIMITED ban on Incineration. - Incineration, hereby defined as the burning of municipal, biochemical and hazardous wastes, which process emits poisonous and toxic fumes, is hereby prohibited: Provided, however, that the prohibition shall not apply to STATE-OF THE-ART INCINERATORS USING MODERN TECHNOLOGY WITH A TOLERABLE LEVEL OF TOXIC FUMES EMITTED IN THE PROCESS OF BURNING WASTE, THE USE OF WHICH IS SUBJECT TO PRIOR APPROVAL OF THE CITY GOVERNMENT TASK FORCE CREATED FOR THE PURPOSE TAKING INTO CONSIDERATION THE SAFETY OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND THE HEALTH OF THE PEOPLE: Provided further, that the prohibition shall not apply to traditional small scale method of community/neigh boorhood sanitation "siga", traditional, agricultural, cultural, health and food preparation and crematoria: x x x."

rows.abstract: It is ironic how the government can boast of various gargantuan infrastructure undertakings when in fact, it could not even do the same when it comes to providing public restrooms. For instance, such areas as mass transit stations, waiting sheds, parks and public highways are severely lacking in toilet facilities. Most public places in the country do not even have one.
